thread:
jamie (acct-team): Hey team — customer ACMECorp can't view audit logs after their SSO migration yesterday. Admins can see usage dashboards but when they open Compliance → Audit logs they get a 'Not authorized' UI state. ticket# 4521.
elaine (support): Thanks @jamie — can you paste the exact error they see or a screenshot? also did they change role names or group ids in IdP?
jamie (acct-team): Screenshot: 'You do not have permission to view audit records' — it's the gray empty state with a link to contact support. They did a SAML->OIDC migration and we updated SCIM groups. Role mapping looks same on our end (they map Okta groups -> Redwood roles).
elaine (support): repro steps requested from customer: 1) login via SSO 2) visit /console/orgs/ACMECorp/compliance/audit 3) see empty state. They ran curl against API and got 403. They provided minimal repro: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/{org_id}/audit/logs
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"audit.read not granted for token"}
```
jamie (acct-team): exact. customer says tokens look fine in their IdP.
elaine (support): ok tagging infra/plat for mapping check. @rachel can you check whether the org entitlement check uses OIDC `scope` or `entitlements` claim? customers migrating from SAML->OIDC sometimes lose the entitlement claim.
rachel (plat-engineer): jumping in — for audit read we check two things: (1) the user's role in our org (Admin or Compliance role) and (2) that the token includes the `audit:read` entitlement scope OR the `entitlements` claim contains `audit:read`. Historically SAML SCIM provisioning created org roles, but some OIDC flows expect the IdP to emit `entitlements` claim. If they flipped flows, mapping might not have been recreated.
ivan (security): quick ask — is retention access gated the same way? e.g., if they hit the export endpoint for compliance retention they get 403 as well?
jamie (acct-team): yes, they also reported exports failing with 403: `retention.access denied`. Might be a separate entitlement `audit:export` or `compliance:retention`.
rachel (plat-engineer): right — there are two entitlements: `audit:read` and `audit:export` (exports/retention). UI shows a single empty state but underlying checks are per-endpoint.
elaine (support): can we get a payload of the ID token or access token claims (PII-redacted) from the customer? they said they can't share full token, but can they paste JSON of decoded claims?
jamie (acct-team): customer pasted claims (redacted):
```
{
  "sub": "00u1abcd...",
  "email": "admin@acme.com",
  "groups": ["ACME-Admins"],
  "roles": ["admin"],
  "scope": "openid profile email",
  "azp": "redwood-client"
}
```
elaine (support): aha — no `entitlements` claim and no `audit` scope. they have groups/roles but our runtime uses explicit entitlement checks for audit endpoints. that mismatch is the culprit.
jamie (acct-team): customer says SCIM shows them as `organization_admin` too. why doesn't that suffice?
rachel (plat-engineer): long story: historically we allowed org role alone, but last year we tightened audit endpoints to require explicit entitlements as part of compliance hardening (to avoid accidental access from role sync bugs). We should have surfaced this during onboarding but looks like it slipped.
ivan (security): we made that change intentionally to ensure only audited entitlements are granted. Recommend we do two things: 1) immediate workaround for customer (grant entitlements server-side) 2) longer-term fix: better console UX/warnings and IdP mapping docs.
elaine (support): for immediate fix — we can mint a service-token with `audit:read` + `audit:export` for the affected org and attach it to their session or set a flag on org entitlements. Can we do that safely?
rachel (plat-engineer): yes, we have an org-level entitlement record. I can add `audit:read` & `audit:export` to ACMECorp's org entitlements. Doing this will allow their admins to read logs/export. I'll need approval from security to proceed.
ivan (security): approved for ACMECorp only. Patch the entitlement and add audit log entry for the change. Make sure we don't accidentally grant to all orgs.
rachel (plat-engineer): applying now. command: 
```
# admin CLI (internal)
redwood org update-entitlements --org ACMECorp --add "audit:read,audit:export"
```
-- I'll run in staging first then prod.
deploy-bot: Deployment queued: entitlement-update-2026-03-15-01. staging -> prod pipeline started.
elaine (support): customer confirmed after staging change they could view logs in UI (staging env of console). once prod flips they will confirm. telling them to wait 10m. :thumbsup:
jamie (acct-team): customer confirmed prod now works. thank you.
elaine (support): follow-up items for us: 1) update SSO migration playbook to call out `entitlements` claim requirement; include sample mapping for Okta/OneLogin/Azure. 2) surface a console banner when an org has role but missing audit entitlements. 3) docs update. I'll create tasks.
ivan (security): also open a short-lived audit trail ticket so we can roll back if needed and document why ACMECorp got the entitlement.
rachel (plat-engineer): created infra ticket INF-2789 to add server-side diagnostic to log when a user has admin role but access denied for audit endpoints. will also add a warning in the console.
elaine (support): wrote steps to recommend to customers who want to fix in IdP instead of us granting entitlements:
- For OIDC: ensure the IdP includes `entitlements` claim in access token with values `["audit:read","audit:export"]` OR include `audit:read audit:export` in the `scope` claim.
- For SAML: ensure SCIM provisioning maps the group to Redwood role and include `entitlements` custom attribute mapping if available.
Examples (Okta OIDC claim mapping):
```
// Okta inline mapping example
Token Claims -> Map -> Token Claim Name: entitlements
Value: Array -> Expression: user.groups.contains("ACME-Admins") ? ["audit:read","audit:export"] : []
```
elaine (support): I'm going to add a KB article and ping KB reviewers. @rachel @ivan please review before I publish.
rachel (plat-engineer): will review. small code change planned in console to show missing-entitlement banner (will PR today).
ivan (security): reviewing KB and will add security caveats. also suggest we add a transient check during SSO migration flow to warn customers.
jamie (acct-team): thanks all. customer satisfied. closing ticket after KB published.
elaine (support): closing notes: root cause = SSO->OIDC migration removed explicit `entitlements` claim/scope; fix = org entitlement add OR IdP mapping update. docs + console follow-ups opened. :white_check_mark:
jamie (acct-team): marking resolved on our side.
elaine (support): thanks everyone.
